label: conj:orbital-fourier-decomposition
title: Quantum numbers from Fourier decomposition of normal-bundle sections
html:
Conjecture. Quantum numbers from Fourier decomposition of normal-bundle sections

Let \varrho: S^1 \hookrightarrow \Sigma_4 be the trefoil T_{2,3} embedded in Bring's surface, and let N = N_{\varrho/\Sigma_4} be the normal bundle. The four quantum numbers (n, \ell, m, s) arise directly from the Fourier decomposition of sections \sigma \in \Gamma(N).

At each point of the trefoil, N_p \cong \mathbb{R}^2. Let \varTheta \in [0, 2\pi) parametrise the trefoil. A section decomposes into orthogonal modes:

  \sigma(\varTheta)
  = \sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty} \bigl(a_\ell \cos(\ell\varTheta) + b_\ell \sin(\ell\varTheta)\bigr) \hat{n}_1(\varTheta) +
  \sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty} \bigl(c_\ell \cos(\ell\varTheta) + d_\ell \sin(\ell\varTheta)\bigr) \hat{n}_2(\varTheta)

where \hat{n}_1, \hat{n}_2 form an orthonormal frame for N.

(1) Principal quantum number n. The total twist k = 2(n-1) constrains the total energy E_n = -E_{\mathrm{ion}}/n^2. The twist equates to the L^2 norm-squared of \sigma. At fixed k, only finitely many Fourier modes can be nonzero.

(2) Angular momentum quantum number \ell. The \ell-th Fourier mode acts as a resonance frequency of the trefoil's transverse vibration, carrying eigenvalue \lambda_\ell = [\ell]_q [\ell + 1]_q under the q-Laplacian. The q-deformation shifts the eigenvalues by order \alpha^2, producing fine-structure splitting between sub-shells at the same n.

(3) Magnetic quantum number m. The \mathrm{SO}(3) rotation group acts on \mathbb{R}^3 and the normal-bundle sections. Mode-\ell sections transform as the irreducible representation V_\ell of \mathrm{SO}(3). The magnetic quantum number m = -\ell, \ldots, +\ell labels the weight spaces relative to the Reeb axis.

(4) Spin quantum number s. The fiber adjoint involution acts on the normal bundle by exchanging the two orientations of the Hopf link between electron and proton. This involution \sigma \mapsto -\sigma splits each orbital (n, \ell, m) into two eigenspaces (s = \pm 1/2), doubling the orbital count to 2n^2 states per shell.
